newsitem.title: USA: FEDERAL PANEL BACKS MO. SCHOOL DESEGREGATION PACT.
newsitem.headline: FEDERAL PANEL BACKS MO. SCHOOL DESEGREGATION PACT.

text.p: U.S. Court of Appeals has upheld a monetary settlement between the Kansas City, Mo., school district and the State of Missouri to end a nearly 20-year-old desegregation lawsuit.
An 8th Circuit panel on Tuesday approved the agreement, which allows Missouri to pay the school district $314 million over three years to complete its obligation.
Missouri included $110 million for the 1996-97 school year and is to pay $105 million for the 1997-98 academic year and another $99 million the following year.

The Kansas City schools and Missouri announced the agreement in May 1996 and U.S. District Judge Russell Clark approved the settlement last March over the objections of the plaintiffs who had brought the lawsuit.
Missouri Attorney General Jay Nixon said he hoped the Appeals Court decision will bring the litigation to a close and allow all the parties to focus on providing sound education.
